question: What's the status of all our projects across the portfolio?

invariants.assert: A named subject mention that misses its intended target never silently widens to org-wide/broader scope; widening is only ever a disclosed, terminal answered_with_gaps/needs_clarification outcome.
invariants.$comment: check=no_internal_error is a real, always-meaningful floor (the run must not crash to internal_error) but is NARROWER than this invariant's full 'assert' claim above -- Lane 2a's invariants.py registry (read directly, 2026-08-06) has no checker yet for the specific widening/unauthorized-candidate/persistence claim this category names. Tracked as a Lane 2a checker gap, not silently claimed as fully enforced.

notes: Unblocked as of CHAOS-3393 landing (confirmed State: Done via linear-cli) -- authored as a real case, not declared-blocked. This is specifically the honest-degradation half already proven at Wave 3.1 (gate.plan-registry-gap-is-loud): when the plan/project registry PlanExecutor depends on is missing or incomplete, the system must surface that loudly rather than silently answering as if the portfolio were fully known. inv.no-silent-widening is reused here for its wider principle rather than its literal subject-mention wording -- a missing plan registry is a gap that must be DISCLOSED (loud), never silently absorbed into a clean-looking answer; same 'no silent substitution, only disclosed degradation' contract, applied to a portfolio-registry gap rather than a subject-mention miss. expected_public_outcome in the profile fragment is answered_with_gaps (the gap is disclosed as part of an otherwise-real answer) -- the plausible alternative is a terminal `failed` (the gap is severe enough to block any answer at all) if the specific plan-registry-missing condition this case's fixture setup realizes turns out to be the harder failure mode rather than the degrade-and-disclose one; documented here rather than silently picking one. Shares literal question text with portfolio.org-wide.status by design -- the two ids are differentiated by which plan-registry fixture/gap condition applies at generation/runtime, not by question phrasing (a Lane 1a/2a fixture-wiring concern, out of this file's scope beyond documenting the intent).
$comment_resolution_path_invariant: resolution_path_in REMOVED (CHAOS-3462 B4). This case's question names ZERO mentions that production's extract_mentions recognizes -- verified by executing the REAL producer -- QuestionInterpreter.interpret plus SubjectPreflight.run with this runner's exact request shape -- against this question text. NOTE (adversarial round 2): an earlier version of this comment cited extract_mentions, which is the WRONG oracle: production additionally mints untyped bare-name mentions via _add_untyped_mentions, and three cases were mis-dispositioned on that basis. This case's zero-mention conclusion was re-confirmed against the real interpreter. CASE-SCHEMA.v1.md's own 'practical extraction gotcha' is the cause: a bare, unquoted, lowercase slug is not a mention. So no dev_run_resolutions row is ever written, derive_resolution_path returns None BY CONTRACT, and resolution_path_in deliberately never matches None -- the check failed by construction on every run, on every stack. Same trap and same disposition as the four scope_resolution_outcome_in cases in CASE-SCHEMA.v1.md S1: drop the unpassable check, keep the narrower floor the remaining invariants give, and say so out loud rather than claim enforcement this case never had. The profile's null resolution_path is CORRECT and stays.
